chapter.v:
Later on
the cupbearer and the baker committed some offense against their master, the king of Egypt.

Pharaoh was
angry with these two royal officials—the chief cupbearer and chief baker—

and imprisoned
them in the house of the commander of the guard, the same prison where Joseph was.

The commander
of the guard assigned Joseph to them as their personal attendant. They were kept in prison for some time.

One night
while they were in prison the cupbearer and the baker for the king of Egypt each had a dream. They were different dreams, each with its own meaning.

When Joseph
arrived the next morning he noticed they both looked depressed.

So he
asked Pharaoh's officials who were imprisoned with him in his master's house, “Why are you looking so depressed?”

“We've both
had dreams but can't find anyone to explain what they mean,” they said.So Joseph told them, “Isn't God the one who can interpret the meaning of dreams? Tell me your dreams.”

So the
chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream. “In my dream there was a vine right in front of me,” he explained.

“The vine
had three branches. As soon as it budded, it flowered, and produced clusters of ripe grapes.

I was
holding Pharaoh's wine cup, so I picked the grapes and squeezed them into the cup and gave it to Pharaoh.”

“This is
the meaning,” Joseph told him. “The three branches represent three days.

In three
days' time Pharaoh will take you out of prison and give you back your job, and you will hand Pharaoh his cup as you used to.

But when
things go well for you, please remember me with kindness and speak to Pharaoh on my behalf, and please get me out of this prison.

I was
cruelly kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and now I'm here in this pit even though I've done nothing wrong.”

When the
chief baker saw that the interpretation was positive, he said to Joseph, “I also had a dream. I had three baskets of cakes on my head.

In the
top basket were all the cakes and pastries for Pharaoh to eat, and the birds were eating them from the basket on my head.”

“This is
the meaning,” Joseph told him. “The three baskets represent three days.

In three
days' time Pharaoh will take you out of prison and hang you on a pole, and birds will eat your flesh.”

Three days
later it happened to be Pharaoh's birthday, and he arranged a banquet for all his officials. He had the chief cupbearer and the chief baker released from prison and brought there before his officials.

He gave
the chief cupbearer his job back, and he returned to his duties of handing Pharaoh his cup.

But he
hanged the chief baker just as Joseph had said when he interpreted their dreams.

But the
chief cupbearer didn't remember to say anything about Joseph—in fact he forgot all about him.
